What comes up in Austral

3 conditions, and each one is handled differently

Every site is scoped on the day. The table is what the work usually involves here rather than a statement about any particular property.

Clearing a holding for subdivision

House, sheds, old fencing, concrete and accumulated material on a block that is about to become several.

How it is handled
Taken off in sequence with the streams kept apart, then the block left clear and at a workable level for the civil works.
What does it
Midi to large excavator with a grapple, truck and dogs for volume.

Old farm sheds and outbuildings

Steel frames, cement sheet roofing and concrete pads that have been there far longer than the house.

How it is handled
Condition of the sheeting assessed before anything is touched, removed whole where possible, then the frame and the pad taken out.
What does it
Licensed asbestos removalists for the sheeting, then an excavator with a hammer for the pad.

Sheds, garages, pools and outbuildings

Partial demolition, and frequently several structures in one scope with a different waste stream against each.

How it is handled
Taken down separately so the streams stay apart. A pool shell is broken out and removed, then the void is backfilled with suitable material and compacted in layers.
What does it
Mini or midi excavator, a hammer for the pool shell, and tippers rather than a truck and dog on the smaller volumes.

Austral

What shapes the work on these blocks

  • Large semi rural blocks Generous by suburban standards, with room to work and room to separate material on site rather than carting it mixed.
  • Subdivision rather than knockdown rebuild A lot of the work here is clearing a holding ahead of a subdivision, which means sheds and outbuildings as much as houses.
  • Old sheds and farm structures Where fibro sheeting and roofing turn up regularly and are usually the most weathered material on the property.
  • Bulk earthworks after the clearing Because a subdivided block generally needs levels before it needs anything else.

Austral blocks are large enough that the machine is chosen for the work rather than for the gap, and a truck and dog can usually stand and turn. The planning item here is the haul: the distance to a facility licensed to receive a given classification is a real part of the price out this far.

Austral questions

What people ask before we start

We are subdividing. What comes off first?
Structures and anything hazardous in them, then the vegetation and rubbish, then the levels. Doing it in that order means the material streams stay apart and the earthworks are not working around something that is still standing.
Is the fibro in an old shed treated differently from the house?
Not in principle, but often in practice. Shed sheeting has usually been exposed for decades, and badly weathered cement sheet may have to be handled as friable rather than bonded, which means a higher licence class and tighter controls.
Can you bring fill in as well as take spoil out?
Yes, and where both are needed the same truck movement does two jobs. Clean fill, virgin excavated natural material and road base are supplied and placed, compacted in layers rather than tipped and spread.
Is Max licensed for the asbestos removal itself?
Max holds the demolition licence, AD214737. The asbestos removal is carried out by licensed asbestos removalists, and the air monitoring and clearance by an independent licensed assessor. The whole pathway is managed as one job so you are not coordinating three contractors.
